summary.en: Placed the Ionian Islands under the exclusive protection of Britain as the United States of the Ionian Islands, a nominally sovereign state run by a British Lord High Commissioner.
Declared Greece an independent state under the guarantee of the three Powers. The frontier it drew, along the Aspropotamos and Spercheios rivers, was narrower than the line finally agreed in 1832.
The Ottoman Empire recognised the independent Kingdom of Greece and accepted a frontier from the Gulf of Arta to the Gulf of Volos, in return for an indemnity.
Britain ceded the Ionian Islands to Greece on condition of their perpetual neutrality. The transfer took effect on 2 June 1864.

Britain took over the administration of Cyprus in return for a defensive alliance against Russia. Ottoman sovereignty was preserved on paper until Britain annexed the island on the outbreak of war with the Ottoman Empire in November 1914.
Following the Congress of Berlin, the Ottoman Empire ceded Thessaly and the district of Arta to Greece. Elassona and Preveza stayed Ottoman.
Ended the First Balkan War. The Ottoman Empire gave up all its European territory west of a line from Enos to Midia, and left the fate of the Aegean islands and of Albania to the Great Powers.
Ended the Second Balkan War and divided Ottoman Macedonia. Greece received southern Macedonia with Thessaloniki and Kavala; Bulgaria kept an outlet to the Aegean in Western Thrace.
The peace with Bulgaria after the First World War. Bulgaria ceded Western Thrace to the Allied Powers, who passed it to Greece in May 1920.
Awarded Greece Eastern Thrace and the administration of the Smyrna zone, with a plebiscite on sovereignty after five years. Never ratified, and overtaken by the Turkish victory of 1922.
Ended the fighting in Anatolia and required Greece to evacuate Eastern Thrace within thirty days, ahead of the settlement at Lausanne.

Replaced Sèvres. Fixed the Greek-Turkish frontier on the Evros, returned Eastern Thrace, Imbros and Tenedos to Turkey, and gave the Dodecanese to Italy. The convention on the exchange of populations was signed alongside it in January.
The peace with Italy after the Second World War. Italy ceded the Dodecanese to Greece; the formal union followed on 7 March 1948.
Settled the constitution and guarantee of an independent Cyprus. The Republic was proclaimed on 16 August 1960, with Britain retaining two sovereign base areas.
